core_obligations: Record that being an open immersion is stable under base change and Zariski local on the base (proof lines 6085-6088).
Reduce to a flat surjective morphism of affines and deduce that f is universally open and universally injective (proof lines 6090-6099).
Use openness of f(X) and shrink to affine opens U of the image, reducing further to the case where f' is an isomorphism (proof lines 6100-6107).
In the isomorphism case, show that f is a bijective homeomorphism, hence affine, and conclude that O(S) -> O(X) is an isomorphism by faithful flatness of O(S) -> O(S') (proof lines 6109-6127).
Apply the general descending-properties-morphisms lemma to finish (proof line 6128).
proof_roadmap: Second reduction to the isomorphism case (proof lines 6100-6107).
The isomorphism case by faithful flatness (proof lines 6109-6127).
Conclusion by the general descending-properties lemma (proof line 6128).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property 'f is an open immersion' is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 6078-6082). The proof first records base-change stability and Zariski locality, then reduces to a single flat surjective morphism of affine schemes S' -> S whose base change f' is an open immersion: f is shown to be universally open and universally injective by the two corresponding descent lemmas, hence f(X) is open, and the problem is further reduced to the case where f' is an isomorphism by shrinking to affine opens U of the image; in that case f is surjective, universally injective and universally open, hence a bijective homeomorphism, hence affine by the homeomorphism-affine lemma, and the isomorphism is then detected by faithfully flat descent of the ring map O(S) -> O(S') (proof lines 6084-6128). The level is H3: two nested reductions and a genuinely displayed final ring-theoretic step, ending with the general descending-properties-morphisms lemma.
